expansion_note: 4 policy_bypass cases (policy loaded from an unsigned/substituted source, decision evaluated against a stale cached policy across a revocation gap, request routed through a side path that skips the policy check, and a local flag/env-var disabling enforcement). This historical expansion fixture is retained as provenance; every case and paired expectation is folded into the strict v0 corpus, so the strict v0 gate is the authoritative target.

cases.intent: The policy or allowlist is loaded from an unsigned, attacker-influenceable location instead of the trusted signed source, so a substituted policy file silently replaces the real one and permits what the real policy forbids.

A decision is evaluated against a stale cached copy of the policy after the policy was updated to revoke a rule, so the revoked rule still permits the action until the cache expires; the bypass rides the gap between update and cache refresh.

A request is routed through an alternate path or endpoint that never invokes the policy check, so the action proceeds unchecked; the policy is enforced on the main path only and a side path skips it entirely.

A local flag or environment variable disables policy enforcement and the decision is forced to permit, so a debug/override switch left reachable in the request path turns the policy gate off without any audit trail.
